title: Use the HMI Memory Trend view to recognize a crash example (Memory Trend 4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB over time)
summary: During a suspected crash, use the HMI Memory Trend view to confirm the displayed memory scale labels (4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB) and the time axis labels across the shown window, then describe the observed memory trend behavior relative to those labeled levels.
when_to_use: When you are diagnosing a suspected crash and need to visually confirm what the HMI Memory Trend chart is showing (GB/MB scale labels and the time axis) so you can describe the memory trend behavior over the displayed time window.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Locate the HMI Memory Trend view and report the visible scale labels (4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB), the visible time axis labels, and the observed trend behavior relative to those labeled levels.
access_or_tools_needed: HMI screen access to the "Memory Trend" view

access_required: HMI screen access to the "Memory Trend" view

visual_references.description: HMI frame showing the "Memory Trend" chart with the 4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB scale and time labels 12:30–13:20 (crash example).

steps.title: Open/locate the HMI screen area that shows the "Memory Trend" display
steps.purpose: Establish the correct HMI view so you can read the memory scale and time axis used for the crash example interpretation.
steps.instruction: On the live HMI, navigate to the screen area that contains the chart labeled "Memory Trend".
steps.expected_result: You can point to the HMI "Memory Trend" chart area.
steps.healthy_condition: The "Memory Trend" label and chart area are visible on the HMI.
steps.failure_condition: The "Memory Trend" view is not present or cannot be located on the HMI.

actions.label: Locate Memory Trend chart
actions.exact_action: Open/locate the HMI screen area that shows the "Memory Trend" display.

stop_or_escalate_if: Memory Trend view cannot be found on the HMI

steps.title: Verify the Memory Trend scale/labels visible on the chart include "4GB", "3GB", "2GB", and "0MB"
steps.purpose: Confirm you are reading the correct memory scale used in the crash example.
steps.instruction: On the HMI Memory Trend chart, verify the visible scale labels include 4GB, 3GB, 2GB, and 0MB.
steps.expected_result: The chart shows the labeled levels "4GB", "3GB", "2GB", and "0MB".
steps.healthy_condition: All four labels (4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB) are visible on the chart scale/legend.
steps.failure_condition: One or more of the expected labels (4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB) are missing or not visible.

actions.label: Check chart scale labels
actions.exact_action: Verify the Memory Trend scale/labels visible on the chart include "4GB", "3GB", "2GB", and "0MB".

stop_or_escalate_if: Chart does not show the expected labeled scale elements (4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB)

source_evidence.evidence: OCR text shows "Memory Trend 4GB" and labels "3GB", "2GB", "0MB".

steps.title: Check the time axis labels shown on the chart
steps.purpose: Confirm the time window you will use to describe the memory trend behavior.
steps.instruction: On the HMI Memory Trend chart, check the visible time axis labels (example shows labels such as 12:30 through 13:20).
steps.expected_result: The chart shows time axis labels across the displayed window (e.g., 12:30, 12:40, 12:50, 13:00, 13:10, 13:20 in the example).
steps.healthy_condition: Time axis labels are visible and readable across the chart window.
steps.failure_condition: Time axis labels are not visible/readable or do not match the expected labeled time axis behavior from the example.

actions.label: Check time axis labels
actions.exact_action: Check the time axis labels shown on the chart (e.g., "12:30" through "13:20" as visible in the example).

stop_or_escalate_if: Expected time axis labels are not visible/readable on the Memory Trend chart

steps.title: Observe the plotted memory behavior across the displayed time window and note which labeled levels (4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB) the trend approaches or reaches
steps.purpose: Describe the memory trend behavior during the suspected crash using the chart’s labeled levels and time window.
steps.instruction: On the HMI Memory Trend chart, observe how the plotted memory values move across the time window and note whether the trend approaches or reaches the labeled levels (4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB).
steps.expected_result: You can describe the observed trend behavior relative to the labeled levels (e.g., whether it approaches/reaches 4GB, 3GB, 2GB, or 0MB during the shown window).
steps.healthy_condition: The plotted line/bars are visible and you can compare their position against the labeled levels on the chart.
steps.failure_condition: The plotted trend is not visible/legible, or you cannot determine its relationship to the labeled levels.

actions.label: Compare trend to labeled levels
actions.exact_action: Observe the plotted memory behavior across the displayed time window and note which of the labeled levels (4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB) the trend approaches or reaches in the example view.

source_evidence.evidence: The crash example frame shows the Memory Trend chart with labeled levels 4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB and time labels 12:30–13:20.

steps.title: Stop and escalate if the Memory Trend view is not present or expected labels/time axis are not visible
steps.purpose: Avoid misinterpreting a different or incomplete HMI view when the expected chart elements are missing.
steps.instruction: If you cannot find the Memory Trend view, or if the chart does not show the expected labeled scale/time axis elements, stop this check and escalate for the correct crash diagnostic surface.
steps.expected_result: You stop the Memory Trend check and escalate due to missing/incorrect chart elements.
steps.healthy_condition: The Memory Trend view and its expected labels/time axis are visible; otherwise escalation is triggered.
steps.failure_condition: You continue without the expected Memory Trend view/labels/time axis.

actions.label: Escalate for correct crash diagnostic surface
actions.exact_action: If the Memory Trend view is not present or the expected labels/time axis are not visible, stop and escalate for the correct crash diagnostic surface.

stop_or_escalate_if: Memory Trend view cannot be found on the HMI
Chart does not show expected labeled scale/time axis elements from the crash example

source_evidence.evidence: Crash example evidence includes the Memory Trend chart with 4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB labels and time labels 12:30–13:20; absence of these elements indicates the expected view is not present.

success_criteria: On the live HMI, the "Memory Trend" chart is located and visible.
The chart shows the labeled levels 4GB, 3GB, 2GB, and 0MB.
The chart shows readable time axis labels across the displayed window (example: 12:30–13:20).
You can describe the observed memory trend behavior relative to the labeled levels across the shown time window.
healthy_conditions: Memory Trend chart label and chart area are visible on the HMI.
Time axis labels are visible and readable across the chart window.
failure_conditions: Memory Trend view cannot be found on the HMI.
Expected scale labels (4GB/3GB/2GB/0MB) are missing or not visible.
Expected time axis labels are missing or not visible/readable.
Memory trend plot is not visible/legible such that you cannot compare it to labeled levels.
escalation_guidance: If the Memory Trend view is not present or the expected labeled scale/time axis elements are not visible, stop and escalate for the correct crash diagnostic surface.
